doc.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Woody Herman charts and the offer to join
summary: He wrote Blame Boehm and Mulligan Tawny for Woody Herman; he was asked to join the band but could not.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: The next one was the one I mentioned about Woody Herman. So I‟ve got a different – you asked if there was a different session. Here‟s one that‟s from May of ‟54. Some of the personnel on here: Bill Perkins, Jerry Coker. As I mentioned earlier, Panama Francis, playing drums.
Those are the two that are credited to you. There‟s a third, The Third Herd (Cohn‟s Alley), which is credited to AC.
So, working with Woody. What‟s working with Woody like? Were you joining the group? Or were you just on these sessions?
I wasn‟t there. They were probably done in New York.

They did call me to join the band sometime around then, but I couldn‟t. I had some stuff going on at home, which was a drag, because I always wanted to play with that band. I envisioned Woody to be a leader like Charlie Barnet, and I‟d liked Charlie so much.
